feedback_interpretation: H40 is revised: m27 completion increases from 8.50 ml at 1/1 to 14.63 at 10/1, rejecting the forecast decrease over that interval, then falls to 7.09 at matched 20/1. This different sampled reversal remains unreplicated. m170 develops later onset growth, reaching 8.43/21.09 ml at 20/1; its comparatively accurate historical predictions and connected curve lower routine expansion priority. H41 supports differentiated joint growth: m51 reaches 26.24/55.67 ml at 10/1 and 150 ul, substantially below its historical 42.83/67.34 forecast; m203 reaches only 12.97/22.33 under its own injection conditions. This supports structural and slope differentiation without isolating a hydroxyl-topology cause. H42 is substantially answered: m6 onset stays shallow as completion grows, and m71 completion increases gently rather than showing a sharp delayed transition. H43 is answered through 20/1: both m188 and m192 mainly grow in completion. H44 rejects the forecast m91 decline: completion rises 7.98/11.12/13.30 ml across 2/1, 5/1 and 20/1, while m74 grows toward much larger higher-ratio endpoints. Their opposite historical error patterns reject a shared diester correction. Earlier m75 and m32 repeats continue to weaken deterministic loading-step and completion-maximum interpretations. H34 remains rejected because its supposed repeat pair contains different molecules. Exceptional m177, m120, m207 and m209 inputs and the isolated m117 near-reversal remain unresolved. Current m18, m202 and m178 cited predictions are ordered, so older reversal flags are retired. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors; selected candidates remain predictions only.
batch_rationale: The latest measurements substantially answer the immediate m170, heteroaromatic, halogenated-aldehyde and fixed-100 ul diester questions. The remaining m27 contrast concerns transfer of a newly measured completion decrease, and the tertiary-alcohol pairs test loading dependence after their steepness differed from historical forecasts. The m74 surface addresses conditional loading around a growing response. Its diester findings also motivate a connected comparison among simpler alpha-bromoesters, including an independently selected methyl/ethyl analogue pair. The m110 and m118 groups investigate ether topology and carbonyl context through controlled curves, while m187 extends aldehyde transfer with a measured endpoint anchor. Two m202 measurements address a distinct represented phosphorus environment efficiently. These comparisons supply interpretable slopes and loading contrasts across ordinary and more polar chemistry.

Increasing EA normally strengthens elution on silica; increasing PE/EA weakens it. Hydroxyl accessibility, carbonyl environment, ether topology and basic nitrogen can alter silica interactions. These priors do not establish monotonic endpoint curves or explain the measured local reversals.
Adsorption nonlinearity, injection focusing, solubility and omitted run or integration variation could contribute to conditional behavior. No supplied measurement identifies which mechanism operates.

Historical residuals indicate previous failures, not current acquisition value. Identical-input repetition addresses persistence; neighboring ratios or loadings address transfer. A repeat alone cannot diagnose optimization, calibration or omitted variables.

expert_synthesis.planner_resolution: Select 32 distinct legal experiments across 12 observed molecular identities. Resolve specific chloroketone, tertiary-alcohol and bromomalonate loading questions, then test transfer across alpha-bromoesters, ether topology, methoxyaldehyde, halogenated aldehyde and the supplied formally charged phosphorus environment. Allocation follows these scientific comparisons without adviser quotas.

selected_plan.batch_strategy: Freeze these 32 current-pool IDs with their supplied predictions before measurement. Each complete molecule/condition tuple is distinct; there are no intentional identical-input repeats. The m74 selections complete a two-ratio, three-loading surface with observed anchors. Other groups form controlled ratio sequences or loading bridges. Preserve density, sample volume, loading-solvent identity and plug volume exactly; sample volume and mass remain coupled. Cross-molecule comparisons retain injection differences. Analyze V1 and V2 separately; V2 minus V1 is elution interval width, not uncertainty.

choices.reason: m27 at 2/1, 100 ul anchors a fixed-loading sequence and contrasts with measured 50 ul before its sampled completion elevation.
m27 at 10/1, 100 ul tests loading transfer of the measured 50 ul completion elevation while holding density and DCM 300 ul fixed.
m27 at 20/1, 100 ul completes the controlled contrast, distinguishing a transferred completion decrease from localization to the existing 50 ul inputs.
m51 at 1/1, 50 ul supplies the lower-ratio baseline beside its measured 2/1 anchor, allowing comparison with the newly measured 150 ul curve.
m51 at 10/1, 50 ul completes the lower-loading ratio comparison and tests whether its strong joint growth changes with loading after excessive historical slope predictions.
m203 at 2/1, 50 ul connects to measured 5/1 at the same loading and directly contrasts with its new 150 ul baseline.
m203 at 10/1, 50 ul completes a matched 2/1-to-5/1-to-10/1 curve, testing whether its moderate tertiary-alcohol response transfers across loading.
m74 at 5/1, 50 ul extends its measured low-loading 2/1 anchor and contrasts with the new 100 ul completion response.
m74 at 10/1, 50 ul tests whether the measured positive loading association at 2/1 persists as both endpoints grow.
m74 at 5/1, 150 ul brackets the measured 100 ul input with selected 50 ul, testing the nearly invariant predicted loading response.
m74 at 10/1, 150 ul completes the two-ratio, three-loading surface, separating onset and completion interactions from local loading invariance.
tert-Butyl alpha-bromoester m46 at 2/1, 100 ul supplies a loading bridge to measured 150 ul and anchors a controlled monoester curve.
m46 at 10/1, 100 ul measures the intermediate ratio response, testing transfer from ordinary bromoesters without inheriting bromomalonate's polycarbonyl slope.
m46 at 20/1, 100 ul completes the fixed-loading sequence and distinguishes shallow response from later onset or completion growth.
Ethyl alpha-disubstituted bromoester m76 at 2/1, 50 ul supplies the lower-ratio anchor for its measured 10/1 input and the selected methyl-ester comparison.
m76 at 20/1, 50 ul completes a controlled sequence through measured 10/1, testing whether alpha substitution preserves modest endpoint progression.
Methyl analogue m93 at 2/1, 50 ul anchors its own curve under PE 300 ul, providing an alkoxy-group comparison with m76 while retaining density differences.
m93 at 20/1, 50 ul connects selected 2/1 to its measured 50/1 endpoint and tests whether its ratio slope resembles the ethyl analogue.
Ethyl bromoacetate m79 at 2/1, 100 ul connects measured 1/1 and 5/1 anchors, extending the monoester comparison to an unsubstituted alpha carbon.
m79 at 10/1, 100 ul connects measured 5/1 and 50/1 at fixed loading and contrasts with its existing 150 ul observation.
Trimethoxybenzene m110 at 1/1, 150 ul extends its measured pure-EA baseline, establishing a controlled test of the predicted completion shoulder.
m110 at 2/1, 150 ul tests the predicted intermediate completion elevation before selected 5/1, with onset and completion assessed independently.
m110 at 5/1, 150 ul distinguishes the predicted completion decrease from continued growth after the earlier m116 decline prediction failed.
m110 at 5/1, 50 ul provides a direct loading contrast and connects to measured 10/1 at 50 ul, making the mixed-loading ether evidence interpretable.
Methoxybenzaldehyde m118 at 1/1, 150 ul establishes an ordinary ether/carbonyl baseline for a controlled curve beyond its single measured 100 ul anchor.
m118 at 2/1, 150 ul supplies a loading bridge to measured 100 ul and the first matched increment in its selected sequence.
m118 at 5/1, 150 ul locates intermediate growth, testing whether methoxy-aldehyde transfer is chiefly completion-dominated or involves both endpoints.
m118 at 10/1, 150 ul completes the controlled curve, constraining transfer from measured methoxy ketones and methylthio aldehyde without imposing a shared response.
Brominated trifluoromethyl aldehyde m187 at 2/1, 150 ul anchors a controlled connection to its measured early-onset 20/1 input.
m187 at 10/1, 150 ul locates the intermediate response, testing structural limits of the newly established m188/m192 completion-dominated regime.
m202 at pure EA, 50 ul establishes a lower-ratio baseline for the supplied formally P-positive structure, whose lone measured anchor leaves its response slope unresolved.
m202 at 10/1, 50 ul completes the fixed-loading ratio contrast and directly compares with measured 150 ul. Its current ordered prediction supplies no reversal-based rationale.

hypotheses.content: m27 has a sampled completion elevation at 10/1 followed by a decrease at 20/1 under 50 ul loading, with comparatively stable onset. Transfer across loading and persistence of either input remain separate unresolved questions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A connected 100 ul sequence distinguishes a transferable completion-shape interaction from localization to existing labels, without spreading the short 20/1 interval across chloroketone chemistry.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 100 ul, does completion increase from 2/1 to 10/1 and then decrease at 20/1, or follow a different progression?

hypotheses.content: Tertiary-alcohol loading effects may change with ratio and endpoint. m51 already shows an onset loading association at 2/1, while m203 completion is close across loading at 5/1. Their differentiated 150 ul curves do not establish lower-loading slopes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Parallel lower-loading curves separate structural response magnitude from conditional loading effects and constrain excessive transfer of steep alcohol slopes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m51 retain strong joint growth at 50 ul, and does m203 preserve its more moderate progression across the matched 2/1, 5/1 and 10/1 sequence?

hypotheses.content: Alpha-bromoester response may depend on alpha substitution and ester alkoxy environment. Sparse monoester anchors do not determine common onset or completion slopes, and the growing bromomalonate curve cannot establish their response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Linked m46, m76, m93 and m79 curves broaden ordinary ester transfer while separating molecular offsets from ratio sensitivity. Different densities, masses and loading solvents remain explicit inputs.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the selected monoesters remain modest, develop delayed joint growth, or differ mainly in completion; and do methyl and ethyl alpha-disubstituted analogues have similar slopes?

hypotheses.content: m74's measured 50-to-100 ul change at 2/1 is positive for both endpoints, despite nearly invariant current loading predictions. Whether this association persists or changes across its growing 5/1 and 10/1 response is unresolved.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A complete two-ratio, three-loading surface can teach separate endpoint interactions or useful local invariance without importing the unstable m75 loading-step interpretation.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Across 50, 100 and 150 ul, are m74 loading shifts small, smoothly varying, or different between 5/1 and 10/1?

hypotheses.content: Ether topology and carbonyl context delimit response transfer. Measured m116 grows rather than showing its forecast decline, while other ether/carbonyl structures have differentiated slopes. The proposed m110 shoulder and fixed-150 ul m118 progression remain untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled ether and methoxy-aldehyde curves distinguish completion-shape errors from molecular offsets, with an m110 loading bridge and an m118 measured-condition bridge.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m110 completion decrease between 2/1 and 5/1 at 150 ul, and does m118 develop completion-dominated or joint growth across its own matched sequence?

hypotheses.content: The shallow onset established for m188 and m192 through 20/1 need not determine the lower-ratio progression of trifluoromethyl-containing m187. Its single 150 ul 20/1 anchor establishes early onset, without locating the preceding response.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: A controlled m187 sequence tests transfer among halogenated aldehydes with similar broad functionality while allowing distinct onset and completion slopes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At fixed 150 ul, does m187 remain early in onset across 2/1, 10/1 and 20/1 while completion grows?

hypotheses.content: m202's supplied formal P-positive representation warrants separate condition-response evidence. Its modest single 10/1 measurement at 150 ul does not establish lower-ratio behavior or transfer to 50 ul.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two controlled contrasts test molecular and condition transfer for a sparsely measured phosphorus/charge environment without assuming neutral speciation or a universal ionic retention rule.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At 50 ul, are the pure-EA and 10/1 endpoints close, and does the 10/1 result resemble the measured 150 ul anchor?

selected_plan.batch_rationale: The latest measurements substantially answer the immediate m170, heteroaromatic, halogenated-aldehyde and fixed-100 ul diester questions. The remaining m27 contrast concerns transfer of a newly measured completion decrease, and the tertiary-alcohol pairs test loading dependence after their steepness differed from historical forecasts. The m74 surface addresses conditional loading around a growing response. Its diester findings also motivate a connected comparison among simpler alpha-bromoesters, including an independently selected methyl/ethyl analogue pair. The m110 and m118 groups investigate ether topology and carbonyl context through controlled curves, while m187 extends aldehyde transfer with a measured endpoint anchor. Two m202 measurements address a distinct represented phosphorus environment efficiently. These comparisons supply interpretable slopes and loading contrasts across ordinary and more polar chemistry.
selected_plan.expected_learning_value: Expected benefits are improved representation of endpoint-specific ratio slopes, conditional loading effects and structural limits of transfer across 12 identities. The monoester and methoxy-aldehyde curves broaden ordinary condition coverage beyond the repeatedly investigated exceptional surfaces. Small loading shifts would provide useful evidence for local invariance. The m27 extensions can test transfer but cannot establish persistence of the existing completion elevation or decrease. No supplied Row weighting or retrained evaluation supports a numerical accuracy-gain estimate.
selected_plan.feedback_interpretation: H40 is revised: m27 completion increases from 8.50 ml at 1/1 to 14.63 at 10/1, rejecting the forecast decrease over that interval, then falls to 7.09 at matched 20/1. This different sampled reversal remains unreplicated. m170 develops later onset growth, reaching 8.43/21.09 ml at 20/1; its comparatively accurate historical predictions and connected curve lower routine expansion priority. H41 supports differentiated joint growth: m51 reaches 26.24/55.67 ml at 10/1 and 150 ul, substantially below its historical 42.83/67.34 forecast; m203 reaches only 12.97/22.33 under its own injection conditions. This supports structural and slope differentiation without isolating a hydroxyl-topology cause. H42 is substantially answered: m6 onset stays shallow as completion grows, and m71 completion increases gently rather than showing a sharp delayed transition. H43 is answered through 20/1: both m188 and m192 mainly grow in completion. H44 rejects the forecast m91 decline: completion rises 7.98/11.12/13.30 ml across 2/1, 5/1 and 20/1, while m74 grows toward much larger higher-ratio endpoints. Their opposite historical error patterns reject a shared diester correction. Earlier m75 and m32 repeats continue to weaken deterministic loading-step and completion-maximum interpretations. H34 remains rejected because its supposed repeat pair contains different molecules. Exceptional m177, m120, m207 and m209 inputs and the isolated m117 near-reversal remain unresolved. Current m18, m202 and m178 cited predictions are ordered, so older reversal flags are retired. All residuals discussed are historical premeasurement errors; selected candidates remain predictions only.

expert_synthesis.chemistry_takeaways: The latest labels distinguish joint alcohol and diester growth from completion-dominated heteroaromatic and aldehyde responses. The m27 completion decrease occurs after 10/1, contrary to its earlier predicted location. Increasing EA generally strengthens silica elution, but the measured local reversals require endpoint-specific interpretation. Adsorption and focusing remain untested explanations.
